summary.text: 没 is the standardized simplified form of 沒. The common reading méi means “not have”; a contested proposal says the graph was borrowed to write this different word because the words may have sounded alike, while other accounts connect the negative use with 勿, 未, or 有. The sound match and borrowing path remain unverified.

formation.text: The construction of traditional 沒 is disputed. The received 說文 analyzes it as 水 plus 𠬸; later commentary assigns 𠬸 a sound role, while another account describes a hand reaching into water. No inspected early glyph witness resolves these accounts, and the proposed sound component’s reading and historical relation to 沒 are unverified.

history.text: 没 is identified as the standardized simplified form of 沒 and is also classified as a variant. A variant-dictionary account says the right side of a common form was often corrupted into 殳. This supports a corruption account for that variant but does not establish a complete graphic sequence leading to standardized 没. The related 𣳚 is described as stroke-reduced; its cited inscription is undated.

uncertainties.text: The hand-in-water picture and the analysis of 沒 as 水 plus 𠬸 are competing accounts; the graph’s original construction remains unsettled.
Later commentary assigns 𠬸 a sound role, but its reading and historical sound relation to 沒 remain unverified.

The origin and chronology of méi “not have” remain unresolved. One proposal is that the graph used for “sink” or “drown” was borrowed for this different word because the words may have sounded alike; other proposals involve 勿, 未, or 有. No primary evidence establishes the proposed sound match or borrowing path.

senses.text: The received 說文 glosses 沒 as 沈, “sink” or “submerge”; dictionary accounts also record sinking and drowning. These uses are documented, but their earliest attestation and the graph’s original meaning are not established.

Duan Yucai interprets “complete entry into water” as extending to “end” or “exhausted,” citing classical examples. This is his account of a semantic development; the earliest use and chronology are unresolved.

In the common reading méi, 沒 is used for “not have” and “none.” One contested proposal is that the graph used for “sink” or “drown” was borrowed to write this different word because the words may have sounded alike. Other accounts propose connections involving 勿, 未, or 有; the older word’s sound, proposed match, borrowing path, and first use remain unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited examples for “sink” and “end/exhausted” were not independently dated, so earliest attestations remain unresolved.

water

Pictograph of a hand reaching in the water to grab something. Later the meaning shifted to "drown". This meaning is only used when the character is pronouned "mò". When pronounced "méi" (which is much more common), it means "not have". This meaning is a phonetic loan, unrelated to the original meaning.
沈也。从水从𠬸。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *mɯːd): semantic 水 (“water”) + phonetic 𠬛.
Possibly a colloquial variant of 勿 (MC mjut) or 未 (MC mj+jH), which fused with or was influenced by 有 (MC hjuwX); not derived from 沒 (OC *mɯːd, “to dive; to drown”) (Schuessler, 2007).

According to Schuessler (2007), formed from the convergence of two etyma:
* Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mit (“to extinguish”). The i ~ u alternation is a common phenomenon in Sino-Tibetan.
* An etymon meaning "to dive", whence Burmese မြုပ် (mrup, “to sink; to be submerged”), which is a loan from Proto-Mon-Khmer *(b)ləp (“to immerse”) according to Shorto (1972).
Unrelated to etymology 1.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary classifies 没 as a variant of 沒 and says its right side was commonly corrupted from the older right side into 殳. It quotes 《類篇》 for several readings of 没, including 莫勃切 and 莫佩切. This supports a graphic-corruption analysis for 没; it does not establish that simplified 没 originated as a planned phonetic substitution.
evidence.title: [A02151] 沒 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary reports 𣳚 as an attested variant cited from 魏穆纂墓誌 and describes it as a stroke-reduced form; it quotes 《正字通》 as saying the right side was abbreviated and the 殳 form was a corruption. The cited excerpt does not date the tomb inscription, so no date for this attestation is asserted here.
evidence.title: [A02151] 沒 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, digitized 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The transmitted 《說文》 glosses 沒 as 沈 and analyzes it as water plus 𠬸. 段玉裁 revises the gloss to 湛, treats 𠬸 as the sound element, and explains “complete entry into water” as extending to “exhausted/entire”; he cites 《小雅》曷其沒矣 and 《論語》沒階 for the extended sense 盡. This is a historical dictionary account and Qing commentary, not direct proof of the earliest graphic form.
evidence.title: 說文解字「沒」及段玉裁注

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.query: 沒 《廣韻》 莫勃切 沈溺 引申 盡 詩經 曷其沒矣
search_audit.outcome: Opened the ShuoWen page and MOE character entry: the former preserves Duan Yucai’s extension to 盡 and cites 《小雅》 and 《論語》; the latter quotes 《廣韻》/《類篇》 evidence. The cited early texts were not separately dated or independently examined.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the Taiwan MOE variant dictionary and Shuowen entry. The Academia Sinica query page showed only its interface, not character-specific forms; no historical image candidate was established.

search_audit.query: Academia Sinica 小學堂 沒 字形演變 版權聲明 CC0
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the database guide and official homepage. The guide confirms database scope, but the character page did not render glyph data and direct attempts to open rights-page URLs failed. No specific image candidate or rights link could be verified.

gaps: No visually inspected oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, or Qin glyph sequence for 沒 was obtained. A search-result excerpt says oracle-bone and bronze forms are unattested, but that claim remains secondary and unverified from the cited paleographic reference.

The received 《說文》 component 𠬸 is assigned a sound role by 段玉裁, but its pronunciation and historical sound relation to 沒 were not independently established. Local Baxter–Sagart data has no 𠬸 row; do not state a confirmed sound match.

The dossier’s pictograph/hand-reaching-in-water account conflicts with the transmitted 《說文》 plus 段注 sound analysis and the MOE corruption account. The early graph cannot be adjudicated without inspected paleographic witnesses.

The physical sense “sink/drown” and later “end/exhaust” are supported as dictionary/source assertions, but exact earliest dated attestations were not established. The 《世說新語》 example surfaced only in a blocked search result.

The origin and chronology of méi “not have” remain unresolved. Proposed phonetic loan, convergence, or influence from 勿/未/有 accounts need primary textual and phonological substantiation; no modern or reconstructed host reading should be substituted for a component reading.
The official Unicode individual record pages for U+6C92 and U+6CA1 were inaccessible. Current readings are locally checked, but no externally verified individual-record click-through is supplied.
No reuse-license review was conducted for any recurring corpus source; no extract recommendation is made.

No verified direct historical glyph-image URL with character-specific provenance and reuse terms was found in this run, so no glyph is proposed. The character-specific Academia Sinica interface failed to expose a glyph record; the MOE page has hand-glyph reproductions but states site-wide All Rights Reserved.

The transmitted 《說文》 account and 段玉裁’s component analysis conflict with the dossier’s hand-reaching-in-water pictograph account. No inspected early paleographic witness in this run settles the graph’s origin.

The sound role assigned to 𠬸 by 段玉裁 is a source assertion; its pronunciation and historical comparison to 沒 remain unverified. The MOE discussion supports corruption in the later 没 form but does not establish original component phonology.

The physical sense and extension to “end/exhaust” have historical-dictionary support, but earliest dated attestations were not independently established. No chronology is inferred from dictionary gloss order.

The origin and chronology of méi “not have” remain unresolved; this run found no primary evidence establishing a phonetic-loan pathway or first attestation. No claim is made about the name or pronunciation of any depicted object.
No official Unihan individual character record or exact local Baxter–Sagart rows were rechecked in this run; the dossier’s reported local reading data remains unverified here.

limitations.text: No character-specific early glyph image establishes 沒’s original construction. The transmitted 說文 account analyzes it as 水 plus 𠬸, later commentary treats 𠬸 as a sound element, and another account describes a hand reaching into water; these explanations remain unresolved without an inspected early glyph witness.
